why_ai: Licensed physicians examine and treat patients in person, carry personal liability, and patients choose and stay with a doctor they trust.
why_clarity: Common visits recur by the thousand, but diagnosis is judgement and outcomes surface weeks or years later, often in another organisation's records.
why_digital: Care starts from a patient in the room and is delivered in person by local practices, with telehealth and records work on the margin.

why_ai: Drafting notes and suggesting codes is screen work AI scribes already do, and EHRs now bundle it free; the signing physician keeps the liability.
why_clarity: E/M and risk-adjustment rules are codified and every visit is a near-identical case, though audits confirm correctness months later.
why_digital: The work starts from a recorded conversation and the chart and ends as a note and a claim, bought by groups from remote vendors.

why_ai: Savings come from physicians and care teams changing care for patients they know, which needs trust and judgement, while the analytics around it automate.
why_clarity: Settlement rules are written down, but cost and quality outcomes arrive a year late and depend on patients, specialists and hospitals.
why_digital: Claims feeds and gap lists are data, but the value is delivered in visits and calls to local patients, through local practice networks.

why_ai: Reading faxed packets, checking insurance and booking first visits is document work agents are taking over; urgency triage still needs a nurse.
why_clarity: A complete referral and a booked visit are checkable outcomes, repeated hundreds of times a week with a written checklist.
why_digital: Input is fax and records, worked on screen, with the patient booked by phone or text by a local practice.

why_ai: Medicare pays for monthly contact by clinical staff under a physician's supervision, and older patients stay engaged with a person they know.
why_clarity: Billing rules and care-plan elements are codified and repeat every month, though whether care management prevents admissions shows only later.
why_digital: Work is phone calls and care plans built from records, delivered to local, mostly older patients by their own practice.

why_ai: Applying incident-to, supervision and collaboration rules is rule-bound back-office work, though a supervising physician signs and carries the liability.
why_clarity: Each visit either meets the written billing and supervision rules or it does not, across thousands of similar visits.
why_digital: The work runs on schedules, notes, agreements and claims on screen, bought by groups from remote vendors.

why_ai: Vaccine stock is physical and handled in the office, but reconciling it to charts, registries and claims is rule-bound work that software can do.
why_clarity: Every dose has a lot, an eligibility status and a code, so reconciliation is exact, repeated and checkable against counts.
why_digital: Inputs mix fridge counts with EHR, registry and claims data; the reconciliation is screen work bought by small local practices.

why_ai: Requirement checks, evidence matching and submissions are rule lookups and portal work that payer APIs and agents are absorbing.
why_clarity: Criteria are published, requests recur by the dozen per physician per week, and approval or denial comes back within days.
why_digital: Orders, charts and policies are documents worked on screen and submitted electronically, often by remote vendors.

why_ai: Matching chart facts to published imaging and procedure criteria is exactly the document task LLM agents now perform, with the physician only on peer-to-peers.
why_clarity: Each request is decided against written criteria, thousands of similar requests recur, and the payer answers within the federal clock.
why_digital: The work starts from orders, charts and policy PDFs and ends as an electronic submission, often handled remotely.

why_ai: Benefits checks and authorization automate, but choosing a funding path across payers, manufacturers and foundations for a costly drug takes judgement.
why_clarity: The goal is clear and checkable, but each drug, payer and assistance programme has its own path, and funding status changes weekly.
why_digital: Work is benefits data, policies and forms on screen, tied to an in-person infusion schedule at a local practice.

why_ai: Measure extraction, scoring and submission are codified data tasks that registries and AI extraction perform with little human judgement.
why_clarity: Measure specifications define exact numerators and thresholds, the cycle repeats yearly for every clinician, and CMS scores it objectively.
why_digital: Inputs are EHR data and notes, the work is on screen, and submissions go electronically through remote registries.

why_ai: Society-run registries are trusted because clinicians govern them, and MIPS reporting and real-world evidence demand keep them funded.
why_clarity: Measure definitions and harvest procedures are standard and repeat each cycle, though research findings are slower to check.
why_digital: Inputs are EHR extracts, analysis is on screen, and reports and datasets are delivered online to members and life-science clients.

why_ai: Reading and structuring public payer policies is the document task LLMs do directly, so the vendor's moat is its history, not its labour.
why_clarity: Each policy version can be checked against the source document, and thousands of similar policies change on known dates.
why_digital: Payer documents in, structured database out, sold online to remote market-access teams.

why_ai: Survey benchmarks are routine analysis software can produce; the association's brand and member base are what buyers pay for.
why_clarity: Survey methods are documented and repeat annually, with benchmark definitions members agree on.
why_digital: Members submit data online and receive benchmarks through a subscription portal.

why_ai: Benefit verification and enrolment are scripted case work voice agents and automation are taking over, though manufacturers want accountable programme staff.
why_clarity: Each case follows a written programme script with a checkable outcome, repeated across millions of cases.
why_digital: Work runs on payer data, forms and phone calls handled remotely for manufacturers and practices.

why_ai: Routing authorization transactions is network software; the analytics on top is standard reporting that AI tools reproduce.
why_clarity: Transactions are standardised and their outcomes recorded instantly, at national volume.
why_digital: Entirely electronic transactions between remote parties.

why_ai: Internal deal and integration analysts make consequential, ambiguous calls for sponsors and boards, who keep paying for accountable judgement.
why_clarity: Deal models and productivity reports have known shapes, but each acquisition differs and returns show years later.
why_digital: The work is financial and claims data analysed on screen, delivered to an internal leadership team close to the deals.

why_ai: Analysts build forecasts and gap lists that software increasingly automates, but practices sign on with an enabler they trust to share risk.
why_clarity: Settlement rules are codified and repeat each year, but savings results arrive a year late.
why_digital: Claims and EHR data in, reports and lists out, delivered to practices that are often remote from the enabler.

why_ai: Measure development needs statisticians and clinicians accountable to CMS rulemaking, and the payment programmes keep the work funded.
why_clarity: Specifications and testing protocols are documented and cycles repeat yearly, with results reviewed in public comment.
why_digital: Claims data in, technical reports out, under federal contracts awarded through procurement.

why_ai: Physician owners hire a banker they trust for a once-in-a-career sale, and negotiating post-sale terms is adversarial judgement.
why_clarity: Each mandate is bespoke, methods vary by banker, and the deal's quality shows years later in the earn-out and comp model.
why_digital: Financials and data rooms are digital, but mandates are won through relationships and in-person meetings.

why_ai: RVU recommendations carry the profession's accountable judgement in a federal process that will keep needing physician input.
why_clarity: Survey methods are codified and codes recur each cycle, but CMS's acceptance and the value's fairness are contested and slow to settle.
why_digital: Surveys and recommendations are digital, but the committee works through in-person meetings within organised medicine.

why_ai: Networks run on physicians' trust in a local governing group; their reporting automates, their contracting judgement less so.
why_clarity: Quality and contract reports repeat each cycle, but results depend on payers and arrive late.
why_digital: Reports are digital, but membership and contracting are local and relationship-based.

why_ai: Contractor medical directors set coverage with legal effect under CMS, an accountable role the programme will keep.
why_clarity: The LCD process is codified with comment periods, but evidence judgements vary and their effects show slowly.
why_digital: Evidence and policies are documents published online, under jurisdictional CMS contracts.
